sentences.show: He told the army he didn't want to fight. Then he captured 132 men.
It happened on this day in 1918, in France.
Alvin York was a Tennessee farmer. His church opposed all violence.
On his draft card he wrote: "Don't want to fight."
He was drafted anyway. His officers argued with him, Bible in hand, until he agreed.
In the Argonne, German machine guns pinned down his battalion.
17 men were sent behind the German lines. Six were killed.
York kept firing. He said later: "I didn't want to kill any more than I had to."
A German officer emptied his pistol at him, missed, and surrendered.
York and seven men marched back with 132 prisoners.
His general: "I hear you captured the whole German army."
York answered: "No sir. I got only 132."
Also on this day: Stephenson's Rocket won the race that shaped railways, and the Great Chicago Fire began.
